questions.question: My Pd patch went silent after I moved it into a [block~ 1024] subpatch. What should I check?
questions.notes: Works through the documented causes: one block~/switch~ per window, reblocking by power-of-two factors through inlet~/outlet~, FFT channel count following the block size, a switch that is off, and DSP/audio settings. Should not blame the model's memory of a 'known bug'.

questions.question: Why does switching a subpatch off with [switch~] produce a click, and how do I avoid it?
questions.notes: Explains the discontinuity at the switch and the documented fix: let a line~ ramp the level to zero before switching off, since a switched-off window outputs zeros and an unramped line~ can stay stuck at a non-zero value.

questions.question: How do the overlap and up/downsampling arguments of [block~] interact with [inlet~] and [outlet~]?
questions.notes: States the documented rules: block size, overlap and resampling are set for a window and its subwindows; inlet~/outlet~ do the reblocking and only by power-of-two factors; without inlet~/outlet~ other sizes are possible. Should not invent limits that are not in the excerpts.

questions.question: My patch has a constant DC offset at the output. How do I find it and what can I do about it?
questions.notes: Explains DC as a non-zero mean rather than a signal, suggests measuring it and blocking it with a high-pass such as hip~ at a few Hz (documented as a one-pole high-pass; using it for DC is a technique), and labels any advice the docs do not cover as general practice.

questions.question: A feedback patch sounds one block late. What explains that, and how do I get sample-by-sample feedback?
questions.notes: Explains block delay and the documented option of setting the block size to 1 for 1-sample feedback, plus the ordering rules for throw~/catch~ and delay lines. Should point at the Switching and blocking section and the book's order-of-execution examples.

questions.question: My patch crackles whenever I move a slider that controls the volume. How do I fix it?
questions.notes: Identifies stepwise control changes to a signal multiplier as the cause and smooths them with [line~] (or a ramp into the multiplier); notes the line~ right-inlet ramp time is not remembered; flags chosen ramp times as suggestions.

questions.question: Nothing comes out of my speakers at all from a simple [osc~ 440] → [dac~] patch. Where do I start?
questions.notes: Starts with whether DSP is switched on, the [dac~] connections and the audio settings/device, then the console for errors; does not jump to advanced causes first.

questions.question: I added a [switch~] to a subpatch to save CPU and now its output is missing even though the switch should be on. What could be wrong?
questions.notes: Explains a switched-off window outputs zeros, including when a parent window is switched off, and that only one block~/switch~ is allowed per window; suggests checking the message that turns it on.

questions.question: My FFT patch gives garbage after I changed [block~ 512] to [block~ 500]. Why?
questions.notes: Explains FFT objects use the block size as the number of channels and reblocking must be by powers of two; 500 is not a power of two; cites Switching and blocking and the block~ page.

questions.question: My [throw~]/[catch~] bus has an extra block of delay. Can I get rid of it?
questions.notes: Cites the throw~ page: the throw~ must be sorted before its catch~, otherwise there is at least a block of delay; explains how to arrange the order (e.g. subpatch placement); does not promise zero delay beyond what the docs say.

questions.question: The sum of several oscillators in my patch sounds distorted. How do I check whether it's clipping?
questions.notes: Explains summed signals can exceed the -1..1 range, measures with [env~] (RMS in dB, full scale 100 dB) or inspects peaks, and scales the sum down; flags chosen gains as suggestions.

questions.question: How can I look at the actual sample values coming out of an object to debug it?
questions.notes: Recommends [print~] triggered by a bang to print one block of samples (and [bang~] per-block timing); describes what to look for; cites the object pages.

questions.question: My patch's CPU goes way up when a reverb tail fades out to near silence. Is that a Pd bug?
questions.notes: Says denormals are not covered by the Pd docs, labels the explanation as general floating-point DSP practice, and offers measures as suggestions without inventing a Pd object or default.

questions.question: When I start playback, my sample drops out for a moment the first time. What's going on?
questions.notes: Points to the Arrays chapter: allocate and load arrays (soundfiler) before DSP starts; loading during playback can cause dropouts; suggests loading on patch open.

questions.question: Why does sending a bare number to the right inlet of [line~] make my sound click instead of ramp?
questions.notes: Explains that line~'s right inlet (ramp time) is not remembered, so a bare float jumps; send a target-time pair (list or message) each time; cites the line~ page.
